clue.text: Fish in position around island

indicators.note: the word for position wraps itself about the island's letter

parts.note: a place is a position or spot

explanation.surface: A fish holding its station near some island.
explanation.definitionFit: The plaice is a flatfish common in European waters, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Clerical assistant moving quickly in holy office

parts.note: a PA, personal assistant, does clerical work
pacy means fast-moving

explanation.surface: A church clerk rushing about inside a sacred building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy office' reads like a room in a church; here it is the office held by the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope's position or tenure is a holy office, which is what this word names.

clue.text: Tree in trouble and stunted in this manner

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

indicators.note: stunted means cut short, so the word and loses its last letter

parts.note: thus means in this way

explanation.surface: A tree that has suffered and failed to grow properly as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunted' clips the last letter from 'and', leaving AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailanthus is a genus of fast-growing trees, including the tree of heaven.

clue.text: Gosh, gentleman is hugging a pirate!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh

indicators.note: hugging means holding close, so the title wraps around the letter

parts.note: Sir is a title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: An exclamation as a gentleman embraces a buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a casual British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a privateer or sea raider, especially on the Barbary coast, so a pirate.

clue.text: Stops if shine's going off

indicators.note: going off means going bad or exploding, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Something halts if its gloss deteriorates.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses every letter of 'if shine's', the S included.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish is to stop or end, so the verb forms match: stops and finishes.

clue.text: Cheeky troublemaker has abused internet

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker

indicators.note: abused means misused or mistreated, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A rude mischief-maker has misused the web.
explanation.definitionFit: Impertinent means rude or disrespectful, a close synonym of cheeky.

clue.text: I am getting the thing put away that's seen to be copy

parts.note: contracted, I am becomes I'm
it means the thing referred to
to put away food is to eat it; ate is its past tense

explanation.surface: Someone tidying a thing away so that it's visibly a duplicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' is the informal sense of eating food, giving ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to mimic or reproduce, a verb sense of copy.

clue.text: Ace maybe showing enthusiasm

definitions.meaning: an ace is a playing card, and it may belong to the suit of red ...
putting one's whole spirit into something; courage or zeal

explanation.surface: A star performer who shows real zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' suggests an expert, but it is a playing card, one of whose suits this is.
explanation.definitionFit: A card from that red suit can be an ace; and showing spirit or zeal is having this.

clue.text: 'Cheap' accommodation almost too expensive? Get angry!

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: steep means overpriced
to rage is to become furious

explanation.surface: Fuming that budget lodging is still overpriced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter of STEEP to give STEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest passenger class on a ship, the lowest-cost berths.

clue.text: Attempt by friend not worth considering

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A mate's effort deemed unworthy of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means trivial or meagre, too small to merit attention.

clue.text: Wasted material is soft — dirt taking time to be put outside

indicators.note: the two joined words are placed around the musical letter, enclosing it

parts.note: soil is dirt or earth
p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Waste being soft, mucky stuff left outdoors for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be put outside' says the joined pair goes around the soft letter, so the one-letter piece is not at the end but sits within.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoilage is goods or material that have been spoiled and are lost as waste.

clue.text: Door-to-door operator is able to upset savers

parts.note: can means is able to

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or thrown into disorder, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A doorstep salesman can annoy people who are saving money.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvasser goes from house to house seeking votes or opinions.

clue.text: Presentations of expeditions below the waves?

parts.note: sub, as in submarine, means under the sea
missions are expeditions or assignments

explanation.surface: Talks about undersea voyages.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as SUB MISSIONS, undersea missions.
explanation.definitionFit: Submissions are things put forward or presented for consideration.

clue.text: Plant festival beginning to take off

indicators.note: the beginning, its first letter, is to be taken off the festival word

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

explanation.surface: A plant's festival is just starting to become popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like 'become popular', but removes EASTER's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like flowering garden plant, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Cooked food takes age with hob and griddle broken

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A meal is slow to cook because the hob and griddle are out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg boiled until its yolk is firm is a cooked food.

clue.text: Head of empire, a more forbidding Bostonian perhaps

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: sterner means more severe or forbidding

explanation.surface: An imperial leader, a stricter type from Boston.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US, people from the Northeast such as Boston are called Easterners.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Boston, on America's east coast, is an example of an easterner.

clue.text: Worker, one with something on head in bar

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
I is the Roman numeral one
a cap is worn on the head

explanation.surface: A labourer in a pub with a hat on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the verb or noun for an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a hindrance or impediment, as a bar to progress is.

clue.text: Strong-willed behaviour being slammed as severest sin

indicators.note: being slammed means being hit hard or criticised, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Forceful conduct being harshly condemned as the worst of vices.
explanation.definitionFit: Assertiveness is confident, forceful self-expression, the conduct of a strong-willed person.

clue.text: Reserve copper has little hesitation to be one helping hostages?

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A backup police officer pauses briefly before freeing captives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal, chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who frees hostages saves them, which is what a person who saves others is called.

clue.text: Name of man in European Union taking position? Name's forgotten

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name is left out of the word for position

parts.note: a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: A man in the EU takes a stand but his name slips away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name's forgotten' removes N, for name, from STANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eustace is a traditional male first name.

clue.text: Son, small child appearing to be slippery

parts.note: a kiddy is a young child

explanation.surface: A boy and a toddler who look slippery.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiddy describes a surface likely to make one skid, so slippery.

clue.text: Gets rid of Democrat, politician in America

indicators.note: in places the politician inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: US is the United States of America
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An American party ditches a Democrat lawmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump something is to discard or get rid of it.

clue.text: Initially master has spoken in lesson

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A teacher begins by talking in class.
explanation.definitionFit: The moral of a story is the lesson it teaches.

clue.text: Big drinker with enormous height, as you might say

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
OS, outsize, is the clothing abbreviation for very large
a peak is a high point

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker of great stature, if you like.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is used to flag a figurative expression, meaning in a manner of speaking.

clue.text: String attached to your new material

parts.note: cord is thin string

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A string is attached to your new fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Corduroy is a ridged cotton fabric, an example of a material.

clue.text: Sealed record containing name of old Queen

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the record's letters go around the name

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a recording
Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714

explanation.surface: A sealed recording holds an old monarch's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is canned has been sealed in a tin.

clue.text: Significant star and mate ultimately put into separate camps

parts.note: Polaris, the Pole Star, is important for navigation

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A celebrity and their partner end up driving people apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Significant star' hints at a celebrity, but it is the North Star.
explanation.definitionFit: To polarise is to divide opinion into two opposing groups.

clue.text: Unknown number meeting ahead of time intimately

parts.note: n is used in algebra for an unknown number
early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: An unspecified figure arriving before schedule, and closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly can mean closely, as in nearly related, so intimately in its sense of closeness.
